reviews.review:
Love this Game! I have been playing it since the first early access and I am impressed how far it has come so fast. The developers are super responsive to my feedback and fix things that I find. Playing with a bunch of friends is super fun. I love the giant spaceship overhead and the VR controls are smooth.

The really cool part is how they are making the game so it will automatically give you cinematic shots. That way when I am recording on my end I don't have to make a bunch of edits and it kind of looks like a post-apocalyptic movie. There are some bugs in that feature still but they seem to be building it out and improving it.

It's a steal of a game for $14 and the fact that I can play in VR and my Best friend can play on a PC... Dumb pandemic, he can't get a VR headset due to supply chain right now so playing on desktop with me in VR is cool.

If you're looking for a truly unique sandbox action alien blastin' zombie bashin' VR/Desktop Co-Op experience, well, Alien Dawn is truly checking off all those boxes in bold permanent ink. Every time you try to escape with your life is a new experience and you never play the same way twice. The loot/guns/health/ammo are all random and you have to go out there with your bravery hat on and find it in order to survive. Vast open map with secret areas, tunnels, caves and hidden (REDACTED) labyrinths. Choosing your weapons wisely and conserving ammo where it counts is crucial. You'll have tons of hilariously tense moments that'll make you and your friends laugh and hold your breaths at the same time. Other times you'll hear noises around dark unknown corners and you'll second guess yourself about confronting whatever is hiding there. Every hill you climb, tunnel you traverse, road you take, and encounter you engage with will test you and you'll need to use the environment and resources differently each time.

To conclude: Alien Dawn is the most fun I've had in VR, ever. Get some friends to join you either in VR or on Desktop and you're guaranteed frantic hilarity and tense unique situations while popping zombie heads & limbs with dozens of guns and melee weapons. It's not just a simple zombie shooter, not at all. Trying to escape ALL of the elements in the game is the destination but the journey will always be unforgettable.

My experience in gaming goes back to the first time 'pong' came out. And while I do own Dungeons and Dragons, I'm a surgeon not a gamer. Alien Dawn kind of attracted my attention though. I found this game to be difficult (for me) to reach the goal which is to  call for extraction. Perhaps it's my non-expertise in gaming. Having said that, perhaps it's my mindset as a surgeon to at all costs reach the goal. So I really want to persist in getting better and it just somehow draws me in to put up the fight. It has become as much a game of strategy for me and I like the sense of accomplishment I get by lasting longer and longer against those damn zombies. 

What's cool about the game is I have never crash landed in the same spot and the landscape is definitely cool and realistic. With practice you become much better at finding food, weapons and that damn map. I know eventually, I will reach the goal and get extracted. I have really enjoyed the challenge the developers have put together. You really feel like a Navy Seal finding yourself in a hostile land with no help. Oh, speaking of help, I did get to play simultaneous with others and if you can play it with friends it's a different ballgame than trying to survive by yourself.  It's less of a challenge though if you play with ten people vs by yourself. I bought the game and I'm glad I did to have a place where I can live vicariously through my character. If you think you're tough enough to join the fight I totally recommend it. It's tough but you'll enjoy the fight the more experience you gain from playing. It's not a sissy game. You in?

Best
Lone Ranger

One of the most fun games I've played in a long time! It's like it took all the best things I liked about Day Z and supercharged them and made them into the crux game. The AI camera is a cool feature that I haven't seen in any game before. I know it's early yet so can't wait to see how this game expands and develops into a bigger more complete experience, but keep up the good work!

Its a pain and a struggle to play this in VR. I'd consider this a alpha release, and find it strange that I actually have to pay to play the game in its current state. I couldnt even get into the helicopter at the start map. Skipped it, and went to next map. There I couldnt pick up any items at the beginning.
reviews.developer_response:
Hi X1234 - Lead developer here.

It should be easier to get into the helicopter in the opening screen now, as well as picking up items in the beginning or storing them into your inventory. reviews.review:
There absolutely is potential in this game and with a few worthy updates it could be awesome. But right now i feel its somewhat unintuitive, its not clear how some stuff works, and has this overall roughness feel. 

Gameplay feels unpolished, i "never" can grab what i want from my holsters on the first try, enemy animations are clunky and unnatural and not in a zombielike way.

That being said, the map is quite big, and its quite impressive whats already here for such an early stage of the game.

Graphics and performance where great, audio was fine too.

I wanted to Coop this with my kid but its not currently in a state where he could handle the clunk.

Its an awesome concept, awesome potential, but currently it has some poor gameplay choices and overall clunkyness.

Id recommend this to anyone that wants to support the project, but know that currently its still has a lot of way to go.

Putting a Negative review for now only because Steam has no sideways thumbs.

There is definitely potential here, but the potential of this game is being barred by a very concerning lack of design and polish that will require further time in the cooking pot before they can get addressed. This is by no means a negative against the devs. They are supposedly a two-person team working hard to develop this game to achieve the goals they want. I just cannot recommend this title at this stage, but I would say that the potential and the interaction the devs have been making with the community might be justified enough for you to put some money in to fund the development.

So what about the game?

Currently, the game feels very much like an improved student showcase project done in game school utilizing store assets to create something. Its better than the countless effortless asset flips on steam at least, but there still requires a LOT Of improvements and features for this game to be worth 15 bucks. This might sound harsh, and admittedly I have not played enough of the game to know it very well indepth, but I have spent enough time in game to get a gist of what is going on. The game as it is, exists as two seperate experiences - VR and Desktop.

While it is no doubt VR was the target focus of Alien Dawn, the current iteration of VR has very un-intuitive controls. Backpacks and Vests are two seperate item containers, and trying to manage them requires you to fumble with both of them trying to slot your items into pinpoint precise circles, failing which to do so will drop the item and require you to bend over to pick them up. There is an auto pick up and store option, which often fails and there is no cue or understanding as to why. Did I just out of the slots that hold that type of item? How do I tell?

Meanwhile, playing on desktop mode (pancake) is a very different set of issues. You can easily tell that this game is made for VR because playing on pancake a lot of things don't work as they should in a traditional game setup. There is a hotbar now and assigned keys, and mouse1 automatically uses items, which is always good, but the game still tries to implement the fiddling of bagpack which was already a problem in VR, and now made even worse in desktop mode. There are a few solutions but I won't discuss them here as this is an impressions review not a feedback thread.

As for the general gameplay, its a mixed bag. The concept, the overall high concept, is really good. We don't have enough open world games on VR, much less so coop games with replayability built in mind. The thematics are unique enough. Sure, its still zombies, but when you see the UFO and Grey Martian looking dudes come out at night, it is interesting at least. The sounds and ambience are pretty great actually. At night there is a general sense of fear when you hear the alien sounds and the darkness is so foreboding.

However, the world design is quite a letdown. First off, there are no unique landmarks that are important in open world games for pathfinding. In Half Life 2, we see the Citadel as a towering landmark that acts as a compass and a orientation guide. In other games, mountain ranges, unique cliffs, cities often provide visual landmarks that let you know where you are even without using the map given enough knowledge. None of that exists here. Everything is designed on a flat axis plane and sometimes you get a slight depression with structures below, or a river, or a small abode. The entire map is a span of vast empty nothing, just rolling green fields and trees, and then the occasional farmhouse that is recycled throughout the map. You don't know what loot is inside them, because everything is so random nothing is ever a tactical decision. A house can have no food, just machineguns laying around. You might find a grenade launcher, but near it are rifle magazines. And this is because there is really not much variation of structure. Almost every loot spot is a repeat of the same farmhouse/whitehouse or military area you just visited minutes ago. 

There are fast travel points, and these aren't even attached to any unique feature or structure. Why is a random grass patch beside the road a fast travel point?? Every spot on the map looks exactly the same, except with a slight variation in how things are arranged. Buildings are singular models and many of them cannot even entered, you can even look at the missing windows and see the insides of the building (Unrendered walls). To get around the map, you require vehicles, which are randomly scattered. There is just so much empty space, and repeating patterns, that there is not much reason to choose to explore one area over another. More interesting POIs and better wayfinding would go a long way if a rework is ever possible. Maps need to have more flair, more character. Have distinct areas of the map that offer different playstyles and objectives. Increase height variation and let the player notice these peaks from far away to aid in navigation.

Guns feel floaty and too much like toys. Enemies are just unpolished generally. Their attacks are too fast without the animation to match, and melee is quite redundant because you take so much damage just trying to melee in desktop mode. There needs to be more guidance on what to do in game.

Now, all this said, its not exactly a bad game. I don't think the devs are trying to make a low effort scam. But as it is, there still needs a lot of work. If anything, the third person desktop mode and the VR mode itself are great areas of potential to work on, and with a redesign of the map, more objectives, better loot distribution and polishing, this game would be pretty decent. I wish the two devs all the best. This review sounds really critical, but they are things a normal player would definitely notice if they are not from the game industry and understanding of development troubles.

Buy to support development, but not to play a game yet as it is still very WIP. There is a LOT of potential here, and with enough work, it will be a good VR game.
reviews.developer_response:
​​​Hi Bottle of Acid - Lead developer here.​

​I first want to thank you for what I can tell is a really thoughtful response to your experience with Alien Dawn. I'm always looking for ways to improve the game from these reviews, both positive and negative, and you being so specific and constructive is very valuable to me.

I'll address your main points below:

"Backpacks and Vests are two separate item containers, and trying to manage them requires you to fumble with both of them trying to slot your items into pinpoint precise circles, failing which to do so will drop the item and require you to bend over to pick them up."

This annoyed me too. It also annoyed watching streamers fumble around with it. To solve this particular issue the collision for the inventory slots is bigger and if you happen to miss the slot, the item will automatically find a spot in your inventory. You can literally just store items in your Vest and Backpack by releasing the item over your body like in mainstream VR games.

Additionally, when grabbing an item out of your inventory, a visible sphere appears to show the exact grip location of the hand you are gripping an inventory item with.

"There is an auto pick up and store option, which often fails and there is no cue or understanding as to why. Did I just out of the slots that hold that type of item? How do I tell?"

The slots are all color coded to different sizes now: Small, Medium, Large and Special.

There is a sound and visual cue to let you know each type of slot is full now.

"...the game still tries to implement the fiddling of bagpack which was already a problem in VR, and now made even worse in desktop mode."

Similar to the VR mode, when you drag an item over the Vest or Backpack it will now find an appropriate slot if you miss the slot when trying to store it. There is also a Holster button for items you're holding (H).

"The concept, the overall high concept, is really good. We don't have enough open world games on VR, much less so coop games with replayability built in mind"

Thank you. I understand your comments, but I appreciate that you get the high concept. And yes, this is exactly why we're making this game. I've read many forum posts (well after we started making this) of people wanting this exact type of game - Open World / Large Group Co-op. We're just trying to make a game us and our friends want to play, and hopefully many more.

"First off, there are no unique landmarks that are important in open world games for pathfinding."

There are more landmarks now than there were when you played in 2021, but I agree, and we want to add much more detail to the open world map. I could go into a lot about this, but in general the issue is keeping the game running properly in VR in an open world, but we're starting to get a handle on that much more now.

"There are fast travel points, and these aren't even attached to any unique feature or structure. Why is a random grass patch beside the road a fast travel point?"

These markets are either Ammo Bases or Radio Towers and should not just be empty in the level.

"There is just so much empty space, and repeating patterns, that there is not much reason to choose to explore one area over another."

While Jes has been the primary designer of the worlds, this is definitely on me. In the beginning it was difficult for me to figure out what exactly was causing the games performance to drop, so we purposely had to keep the design simple. With what I understand now, the worlds should be able to be much more detailed.

"Enemies are just unpolished generally. Their attacks are too fast without the animation to match, and melee is quite redundant because you take so much damage just trying to melee in desktop mode."

The AI will be one of the bigger aspects we focus on in upcoming patches. If they had more life to them I think they game could be really special.

​"Now, all this said, its not exactly a bad game. I don't think the devs are trying to make a low effort scam. "

Thank you. Happy to chat with you any time.

reviews.review:
7/5 stars!

Players can join your game while your in the middle of a match and has a unlockable fast travel after finding a map and clearing military outposts.so you can find eachother over the walkie talkie (you gotta find the walkie talkie as loot as well =D) which is a amazing feature

One of the best VR Co Op experiences i would recommend getting a friend a copy of the game first as lobbies arent always up. All in all great experience! Running over aliens and zombies with vehicles to survive is a must! And the VR driving mechanics are a blast lol

Also since VR and Keyboard players can run together it allows you to connect with friends who cant afford high end graphic cards and VR headsets. 

Please note the devs are constantly working on the game and even a simple suggestion takes hours if not days to implement, more so suggest simple changes to already existing game mechanics and we are sure to see a full release sooner than later!

Fully recommend trying it out with a friend and its a good game without VR in general.

Make sure to join the discord channel for groups
